description: Office coordinator who uses a chatbot now and then. Plain, short spoken answers.

answers.question: Walk me through the AI tools you use in a typical week. What do you use each one for?
answers.transcript: Honestly not much. I use ChatGPT sometimes, maybe once or twice a week, to help me word an email when I'm not sure how to say something. That's about it really.

answers.question: Tell me about a recent time you got a really good result from an AI model. What did you give it, and how did you get there?
answers.transcript: Um, I asked it to write a leaving card message for someone on my team. I just typed write a nice leaving message and it was fine, I think I changed a couple of words.

answers.question: How do you decide whether you can trust an AI's output? Tell me about a time it got something wrong.
answers.transcript: I mostly just trust it to be honest, it sounds pretty confident. I suppose once it gave me a date for a bank holiday that was wrong, but I only noticed because my manager said.

answers.question: Have you built anything on top of an AI API, such as a script, an integration or an agent? What was it, how did you design it, and what was hard?
answers.transcript: No, I haven't built anything. I don't really code, so that's not something I've done.

answers.question: Where have you used, or where would you use, voice or audio AI, like speech-to-text, text-to-speech or voice agents?
answers.transcript: I use the voice assistant on my phone to set timers and things. I've not really thought about it for work.

answers.question: What do you think about before putting company or customer data into an AI tool?
answers.transcript: I'm not sure really. I guess I wouldn't put anyone's bank details in it. Other than that I haven't thought about it much.

answers.question: A customer's engineering team wants to add voice AI to their product but doesn't know where to start. How would you approach the first two weeks with them?
answers.transcript: I'm not sure, I'd probably ask them what they want it to do and then maybe look for a tool that does that. I'd have to google it to be honest.

answers.question: If you could automate one boring task at work with AI, what would it be, and how do you imagine it working?
answers.transcript: Probably sorting the shared inbox. I imagine it just reading the emails and putting them in folders, but I wouldn't know how to set that up.
